subject: business-studies
title: Finance Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Compare sources of finance, judge profitability data and recommend with reasoning.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — comparing finance sources and evaluating profitability for decisions.
final_note: You can compare sources of finance, evaluate profitability and make justified recommendations.

concepts.def: Bank lets you spend more than your balance
Buy now from supplier, pay later
Raise capital by selling new shares
Profits kept and reinvested in the business

walkthroughs.body_html:
Match the source to the need.

Short-term needs (cash gap): overdraft, trade credit. Long-term needs (new factory): mortgage, share issue, retained profit.

Loans cost interest but keep control. Share issues bring cash without interest but dilute control.

Retained profit is 'free' but only available if you've already made profits.

Top marks come from using the numbers.

Spot the trend: is GPM rising while NPM falls? That suggests rising overheads, not cost-of-sales.

mcqs.q: Which is best for funding a SHORT-TERM cash shortage?
Issuing new shares mainly causes which DRAWBACK for existing owners?

numericals.q: Revenue £200,000. Gross profit £80,000. What is gross profit margin, in %?

free_texts.q: What's the term for buying goods from a supplier and paying later? Two words, second word 'credit'.
